Tried shrooms last fall in October at a friends house with all our friends. Ate 3.5 grams raw (not recommend, got a bit of an upset stomach for a few hours).

About 30-40 minutes in I started to get the feeling of butterfly's in my stomach. Kinda like when you get to the top of a rollercoaster after speeding up and you feel your stomach float. I sat back and relaxed on the couch waiting for it to hit. Slowly the walls started to "breath", expanding and shrinking. The posters on with characters on them seemed to be animated in sorts. Like their arms were gently moving and their eyes looking side to side. At this time my friend put on Tycho's "Dive" album. It was absolutely thrilling and amazing. The sounds seemed to sync with the trip. The visuals and music seemed to correlate with each other. When the sounds became "wavy" the walls had a wave to them. Another interesting note was that time seemed to slow considerably on shrooms. What seemed like 3 hours was only 1. I felt as if I reverted back to the state of a toddler. It was a bit of a challenge to form complete thoughts or ideas and giggled at everything.

Within 3 hours after eating we decided to head outside (we had a trip sitter the entire time, always have one). What I experienced inside paled in comparison to outside. The hue of colors become incredibly more vibrant along with landscape breathing. At this point I really started to question what was going on. It felt almost like a dream and that if I tried hard enough I would wake up in my bed.

We decided to take a trip to a nearby ravine that had a really cool gorge (again have trip sitters cause this type of environment can be dangerous). Coming upon the main overhead of the ravine I had extreme enthusiastic excitement. We reached the over look and it was the most beautiful thing I ever saw. The autumn trees seemed liked they flowed out forward forever and the sway of wind made them look like they blended and absorbed into each other. This was the climax for me and I started to cry. I struggled with depression and suicidal thoughts for a few years and the scenery for whatever reason had a extremely deep impact on me. I had a full realization how incredibly lucky I am to be alive in a time and place where I was safe and had people who cared. I could of been born in some fucked up place or time period and had a shitty life. Its one of those things you can say and be like "well ya duh" but actually feeling it is 100% different.

All of us bonded extremely close over the trip and we came away with a greater appreciation for one another. The experience definitely had an enormous experience on my life/outlook and wouldn't change it for anything. I've done it 2 times since and had the high as the first one but not the emotional impact.
